note.question: Does lowering a digital platform commission necessarily induce a content developer to invest more in quality and improve consumer welfare once competing platforms adjust device prices?
note.overview: The paper solves a sequential ecosystem game in which a content developer chooses quality, two device platforms subsequently set hardware prices, and consumers choose a device. Strategic price responses reverse several conventional commission-quality intuitions.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Given an exogenous common commission rate r, the content developer first chooses quality q. Platforms a and b then simultaneously choose device prices p_A and p_B. A unit mass of consumers distributed on a Hotelling line chooses device A or B. The game is solved by backward induction from consumer device demand to platform prices and then developer quality. developer quality precedes platform device pricing platforms monetize both hardware sales and commissions on content

components.label: Subgame-perfect equilibrium of the developer-platform pricing game
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Subgame-perfect equilibrium of the developer-platform pricing game. The developer moves before simultaneous platform device pricing, and consumers determine Hotelling demands after observing prices. The paper solves these stages by backward induction and states interior parameter conditions for the equilibrium used in Lemmas 1-3 and Propositions 1-3.
